exercises.whatItDoes: The back of the knee capsule tightens if the knee rests bent, which is tempting when it's sore. A sustained stretch counteracts that. Our physiotherapists use it most often for total knee replacement, ACL tear and patellar fracture, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit or lie with your heel on a rolled towel or cushion so the back of the knee is unsupported.
Relax and let the knee sag towards straight.
Tighten the thigh muscle every so often to push it straighter.
Hold for 5 to 10 minutes.
Never put a pillow under the knee itself for long periods after surgery.
exercises.howMuch: 5 to 10 minutes, 3 to 4 times a day in early rehab.
commonMistakes: Resting with a pillow under the knee.
Stopping when it feels stiff; mild discomfort is expected.
warnings: Pain becomes severe or calf swelling appears.

faqs.q: Why not rest with a pillow under my knee?
faqs.a: It feels comfortable but lets the knee stiffen in a bent position.

faqs.q: Can I add weight on the thigh?
faqs.a: A light weight above the knee is sometimes used under guidance.

exercises.title: Knee to Chest Stretch
exercises.summary: Knee to chest stretch for lower back pain and stiffness. Single and double knee versions and when to avoid it, from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Bending the lower back opens the spaces at the back of the spine and stretches the muscles along it. People whose pain eases with sitting or leaning forward often find this helpful. You will often see it in our programmes for spinal stenosis, lumbar spondylosis and spondylolisthesis, and it features in our lower back pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent.
Draw one knee towards your chest, holding behind the thigh.
Hold 20 to 30 seconds, then lower and swap legs.
Progress to drawing both knees in together.
Keep your head resting on the floor.
exercises.howMuch: 3 holds each, 1 to 2 times a day.
commonMistakes: Pulling on the shin, which strains the knee. Hold behind the thigh.
Lifting the head.
warnings: Leg pain increases. Some disc problems worsen with bending.

faqs.q: Is this good for a slipped disc?
faqs.a: Not always. Some disc bulges prefer extension. We check which direction helps you.

faqs.q: Can I do it in bed?
faqs.a: Yes, on a firm mattress it's a good way to ease morning stiffness.

exercises.title: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.summary: Levator scapulae stretch for neck and shoulder blade pain. Step-by-step technique and hold times from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Sleeping awkwardly, carrying bags on one shoulder and looking down at a phone all shorten the levator scapulae. The stretch lengthens it along its diagonal line. It is a regular part of rehab plans for cervical spondylosis and torticollis, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit tall and hold the chair seat with your right hand.
Turn your head about 45 degrees to the left, as if looking at your left armpit.
Gently lower your nose towards the armpit.
Rest your left hand on the back of your head to add light weight.
Hold 20 to 30 seconds; you should feel it at the back right of the neck. Switch sides.
exercises.howMuch: 2 to 3 holds per side, twice a day.
commonMistakes: Turning too far or too little. Look towards the armpit.
Letting the right shoulder lift.
warnings: You feel arm tingling or sharp pain rather than a stretch.

faqs.q: How is this different from the trapezius stretch?
faqs.a: The head is turned down towards the armpit, which targets a different muscle further back.

faqs.q: Does it help a stiff neck in the morning?
faqs.a: Often, together with a pillow that keeps the neck in line with the spine.

faqs.q: What is the levator scapulae stretch?
faqs.a: The levator scapulae stretch turns the head towards the armpit and gently lowers it to stretch the muscle running from the neck to the shoulder blade.

faqs.q: How is the levator scapulae stretch performed?
faqs.a: Sit tall and hold the chair seat with your right hand to keep the right shoulder down. Turn your head about 45 degrees to the left, as if looking towards your left armpit. Bend your head forward, bringing the nose towards the armpit. Rest your left hand lightly on the back of your head for a gentle extra pull. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds. You should feel the stretch at the back of the right side of the neck, down towards the shoulder blade.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the levator scapulae stretch?
faqs.a: It relieves the common knot at the top of the shoulder blade, neck stiffness and tension from desk work. It is often part of rehab for cervical spondylosis, torticollis and fibromyalgia syndrome.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the levator scapulae stretch target?
faqs.a: The levator scapulae muscle.

exercises.title: Long Arc Quads
exercises.summary: Long arc quad (seated knee extension) exercise for knee strength. Technique, reps and progression from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Strong quadriceps reduce knee pain in arthritis and make standing, walking and stairs easier. It is a regular part of rehab plans for knee osteoarthritis, total knee replacement and chondromalacia patella, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit upright in a firm chair with feet flat on the floor.
Slowly straighten one knee until the leg is out straight.
Tighten the thigh and hold 3 to 5 seconds.
Lower slowly over 3 seconds.
Add an ankle weight when 15 repetitions become easy.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions each leg, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Swinging the leg.
Leaning back in the chair.
warnings: Pain behind the kneecap increases. We may limit the range.

faqs.q: Is this exercise bad for the kneecap?
faqs.a: In some kneecap problems the last part of the range is irritating. We adjust the range if needed.

faqs.q: Can I watch TV while doing this?
faqs.a: Yes. That's one of its advantages.

exercises.title: Lumbar Rotation Stretch
exercises.summary: Lumbar rotation stretch (knee rolls) for lower back pain. How to do it safely, reps and hold times from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Rotation moves the lumbar joints and stretches the muscles around the spine and hips. The rocking rhythm is often soothing when the back feels locked. It is a regular part of rehab plans for lumbar spondylosis, degenerative disc disease and ankylosing spondylitis, and it features in our lower back pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet together.
Keep your shoulders flat on the floor.
Slowly let both knees fall to one side as far as comfortable.
Return to the middle and repeat to the other side.
For a stretch, hold at the end of the range for 20 seconds.
exercises.howMuch: 10 slow rolls each side, twice a day.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulders lift.
Dropping the knees quickly.
warnings: Rotation causes sharp, catching pain.

faqs.q: Are knee rolls safe with a disc bulge?
faqs.a: Small, gentle rolls usually are. Avoid pushing into big ranges during a flare.

faqs.q: Can I do this after spinal fusion?
faqs.a: Only when your surgeon allows rotation.

exercises.title: Lunges
exercises.summary: Lunge exercise technique for leg strength and balance. Static, reverse and walking lunges from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Split-stance exercises strengthen the front leg's quadriceps and glutes and challenge hip and trunk control. It is a regular part of rehab plans for hamstring strain, quadriceps muscle strain and ACL tear, and it features in our sports physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Start with a static lunge: stand in a long stride with the back heel lifted.
Lower straight down, bending both knees, until the back knee nears the floor.
Keep the front knee over the ankle and trunk upright.
Push back up through the front heel.
Progress to reverse lunges, then walking lunges.
exercises.howMuch: 8 to 12 repetitions each leg, 2 to 3 sets, 2 to 3 days a week.
commonMistakes: Front knee drifting inwards.
Leaning the trunk forward.
warnings: Kneecap pain occurs. Reverse lunges are often easier on the knee.

faqs.q: Forward or reverse lunges?
faqs.a: Reverse lunges are usually more knee-friendly and easier to balance.

faqs.q: I lose balance. What should I do?
faqs.a: Hold a support and shorten your stride.

exercises.title: McKenzie Extension
exercises.summary: McKenzie extension (prone press-up) for disc bulge, sciatica and low back pain. Steps, reps and who should avoid it, from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Repeated backward bending changes pressure within the disc and loads the spine in the opposite direction to sitting. People whose symptoms improve with extension often respond quickly. It is a regular part of rehab plans for disc bulge and degenerative disc disease, and it features in our lower back pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders, as if starting a push-up.
Relax your back and buttocks completely.
Slowly straighten your arms to lift your chest, keeping your hips on the floor.
Go as far as comfortable, pause for a second, then lower.
Earlier stage: rest on your elbows for a minute instead of pressing up fully.
exercises.howMuch: 10 repetitions, several times a day during a flare, as guided by your physiotherapist.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the floor.
Tensing the buttocks and back.
warnings: Pain spreads further down the leg. That's a sign to stop.
You have spinal stenosis or spondylolisthesis; extension may worsen symptoms.

faqs.q: What does centralisation mean?
faqs.a: Leg pain moving back towards the lower back. It's usually a good sign during McKenzie exercises.

faqs.q: Is standing back bending the same?
faqs.a: It's a useful version for work breaks, especially after long sitting.

exercises.title: Median Nerve Glides
exercises.summary: Median nerve glides for carpal tunnel syndrome. Step-by-step sequence and how gently to do them, from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Nerves need to move freely as limbs move. Gentle gliding may reduce nerve sensitivity and improve symptoms. Our physiotherapists use it most often for carpal tunnel syndrome, median nerve injury and cervical spondylosis, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Start with a fist, wrist straight and elbow bent, hand near the shoulder.
Straighten the fingers and thumb.
Bend the wrist back.
Turn the palm up.
Gently move the thumb out to the side.
Hold each stage for 2 seconds, then return to start.
exercises.howMuch: 5 repetitions, 2 to 3 times a day. It should feel mild, never painful.
commonMistakes: Stretching into strong tingling. Glides should be gentle.
warnings: Symptoms increase and last more than a few minutes after.

faqs.q: What's the difference between gliding and stretching a nerve?
faqs.a: Gliding moves the nerve without putting it under tension. Stretching nerves can irritate them.

faqs.q: Should I feel tingling?
faqs.a: Mild, brief tingling can occur. It should settle quickly.

exercises.title: Mini Squats
exercises.summary: Mini squat exercise for knee pain and strength. Depth, technique and reps from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Squatting is a basic pattern for sitting, lifting and stairs. The shallow range limits pressure behind the kneecap while strength builds. You will often see it in our programmes for knee osteoarthritis, total knee replacement and ACL tear, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Stand with feet hip width apart, holding a counter or chair back.
Push your hips back slightly and bend both knees a small amount.
Keep your weight through the heels and knees in line with the second toe.
Hold 2 seconds, then stand up by squeezing your buttocks.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Knees collapsing inwards.
Weight on the toes, pushing knees far over the feet.
warnings: Pain increases the next day rather than settling.

faqs.q: How deep should I go?
faqs.a: Only as far as is comfortable. Depth increases as strength improves.

faqs.q: Can I do mini squats with arthritis?
faqs.a: Yes. Strengthening is one of the most effective treatments for knee arthritis.

exercises.title: Motor Control Exercises
exercises.summary: Motor control exercises for stroke recovery and back pain. What they are and how they're practised, from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Recovery depends on the brain relearning how to control movement. Specific, repeated practice drives that learning. Our physiotherapists use it most often for stroke, cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis, and it features in our neuro physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Break a task into parts, such as reaching to a cup: shoulder lift, elbow straightening, hand opening.
Practise each part slowly with correct form.
Recombine into the full task.
Use feedback such as mirrors, touch cues or video.
Increase speed and complexity as control improves.
exercises.howMuch: Short, frequent sessions daily. High repetition is important.
warnings: Fatigue quickly makes movement worse. Rest and shorten sessions.

faqs.q: How many repetitions are needed?
faqs.a: Many hundreds over time. Recovery is driven by practice.

faqs.q: Is this used for back pain too?
faqs.a: Yes, to retrain trunk muscle control.

exercises.title: Neck Extension Exercise
exercises.summary: Neck extension exercise for stiffness and posture. Seated and prone versions, reps and precautions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Looking up uses the joints at the back of the neck. Controlled extension restores that movement, and the lying version trains the extensor muscles that tire with poor posture. Our physiotherapists use it most often for cervical spondylosis and disc bulge, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Seated version: sit tall, do a small chin tuck, then slowly look up towards the ceiling, keeping the chin slightly tucked so the whole neck moves rather than hinging at the top.
Hold 2 to 3 seconds and return to neutral.
Lying version: lie face down with your forehead on a folded towel. Tuck the chin slightly and lift the forehead a few centimetres off the towel.
Hold 5 seconds and lower slowly.
exercises.howMuch: 10 repetitions, once or twice a day. Build to 3 sets of 10 for the lying version.
commonMistakes: Throwing the head back quickly.
Letting the chin poke forward.
Arching the lower back in the lying version.
warnings: Looking up causes dizziness, visual disturbance or nausea.
You get arm pain or tingling.

faqs.q: Is looking up bad for the neck?
faqs.a: Not in itself. Controlled extension is normal movement. Symptoms like dizziness need assessment before continuing.

faqs.q: Which version should I start with?
faqs.a: The seated version for mobility, the lying version once movement is comfortable and you want strength.

faqs.q: What is the neck extension exercise?
faqs.a: The neck extension exercise is a controlled movement of tilting the head back, or holding against resistance, to mobilise and strengthen the back of the neck.

faqs.q: How is the neck extension exercise performed?
faqs.a: Sit tall and do a small chin tuck first. Keeping the tuck, slowly look up towards the ceiling, letting the movement roll through the neck. Go only as far as is comfortable, pause, then return. Repeat 10 times.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the neck extension exercise?
faqs.a: It restores the ability to look up, counteracts long periods of looking down and supports neck posture. It is often part of rehab for cervical spondylosis and disc bulge.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the neck extension exercise target?
faqs.a: The neck extensors, including the splenius, semispinalis and upper trapezius.

exercises.title: Neck Flexion Stretch
exercises.summary: Neck flexion stretch for tight neck muscles. How to do it safely, how long to hold and when to avoid it, from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: The muscles at the back of the neck work constantly to hold the head up. Gently bending the head forward stretches them and the tissues around the upper spine. Our physiotherapists use it most often for cervical spondylosis, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit upright with both feet flat on the floor.
Slowly lower your chin towards your chest until you feel a stretch at the back of the neck.
For a stronger stretch, rest one hand lightly on the back of your head. Let the weight of the hand do the work; don't pull.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds and breathe normally.
Lift the head slowly back to upright.
exercises.howMuch: Hold 20 to 30 seconds, repeat 2 to 3 times, 2 to 3 times a day.
commonMistakes: Pulling hard on the head.
Rounding the whole back instead of bending the neck.
warnings: Bending the head forward causes electric shock-like sensations down the spine or into the limbs. This needs urgent assessment and the stretch should stop.

faqs.q: Is this safe with cervical myelopathy?
faqs.a: No. People with spinal cord compression in the neck should avoid end-range neck bending unless their specialist advises otherwise.

faqs.q: Should I feel it between the shoulder blades?
faqs.a: Sometimes. The stretch often spreads into the upper back.

faqs.q: What is the neck flexion stretch?
faqs.a: The neck flexion stretch lowers the chin gently towards the chest to stretch the back of the neck.

faqs.q: How is the neck flexion stretch performed?
faqs.a: Sit upright with your feet flat and back supported. Tuck your chin slightly, then slowly lower your chin towards your chest. Stop at a gentle stretch at the back of the neck. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing normally. Lift your head back up slowly. Repeat 2 to 3 times.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the neck flexion stretch?
faqs.a: It eases tightness at the back of the neck and upper back, often felt after long periods of looking up or holding the head still. It is often part of rehab for cervical spondylosis, fibromyalgia syndrome and temporomandibular joint disorder / TMJ.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the neck flexion stretch target?
faqs.a: It stretches the neck extensors, including the upper trapezius, splenius and suboccipital muscles.

exercises.title: Neurodevelopmental Exercises
exercises.summary: Neurodevelopmental exercises (NDT) for cerebral palsy and developmental delay. What sessions involve, from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Guided movement helps the child experience more typical postures and patterns, supporting skills like sitting and standing. Our physiotherapists use it most often for cerebral palsy, down syndrome and infantile hemiparesis, and it features in our pediatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: The therapist positions and supports the child to encourage active movement.
Activities follow developmental stages: head control, rolling, sitting, crawling, standing.
Play motivates movement, such as reaching for toys.
Parents learn handling and positioning for daily routines.
exercises.howMuch: Regular therapy sessions with daily home practice by parents.
warnings: Your child is losing skills they previously had. This needs prompt medical review.

faqs.q: Is NDT evidence-based?
faqs.a: Evidence supports task-specific and goal-directed training most. We combine approaches.

faqs.q: What can parents do?
faqs.a: Positioning, play and handling during daily care make a big difference.

exercises.title: Paralysis Rehabilitation Exercises
exercises.summary: Paralysis rehabilitation exercises for stroke, spinal cord injury and nerve conditions. Home programme guidance from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Movement prevents stiffness, pressure sores and circulation problems, while active exercise builds whatever function is possible. It is a regular part of rehab plans for spinal cord injury, quadriplegia and stroke, and it features in our paralysis physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Passive range of motion for paralysed limbs, taught to carers.
Positioning and pressure relief routines.
Strengthening for muscles with activity.
Breathing exercises.
Transfer and mobility training.
exercises.howMuch: Daily, integrated into care routines.
warnings: Skin redness that doesn't fade, swelling in a limb, or sudden headache with high blood pressure in spinal cord injury.

faqs.q: Can paralysis improve?
faqs.a: It depends on the cause. Therapy maximises whatever recovery is possible.

faqs.q: Do you train family carers?
faqs.a: Yes, as part of home visits.

exercises.title: Parkinson's Exercise Program
exercises.summary: Parkinson's exercise programme: big movements, walking cues, balance and strength. Guidance from Physiosolution neuro physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Exercise may improve walking, balance and daily function in Parkinson's. Large-amplitude movement training counteracts the small, slow movements typical of the condition. You will often see it in our programmes for Parkinson's disease, and it features in our neuro physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Warm up with big arm and leg movements.
Walking with large steps and rhythmic cues.
Balance training: stepping, turning, reaching.
Strength: sit to stand, squats, band work.
Posture: thoracic extension and chest stretches.
exercises.howMuch: Most days of the week, with a mix of aerobic, strength and balance work.
warnings: Falls increase or freezing episodes become more frequent.

faqs.q: When should I start?
faqs.a: As early as possible after diagnosis.

faqs.q: Does medication timing matter?
faqs.a: Exercise is usually easier when medication is working well.

exercises.title: Passive, Assisted and Active Range of Motion
exercises.summary: Passive, active-assisted and active range of motion exercises for paralysis, stroke and bedridden patients. Guidance from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Joints that don't move stiffen, muscles shorten and skin tightens. Regular range of motion work maintains flexibility and comfort, and prepares the limb for active use. Our physiotherapists use it most often for stroke, quadriplegia and Guillain-Barré syndrome, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Passive: the carer supports the limb above and below the joint and moves it slowly through its comfortable range, e.g. bending and straightening the elbow, knee and hip.
Assisted: the person tries to move while the carer or a strap helps complete the movement.
Active: the person moves the joint unaided.
Move each joint slowly, 10 times, never forcing.
exercises.howMuch: Once or twice a day for every affected joint.
warnings: A joint becomes swollen, hot or painful. Heterotopic ossification or injury needs checking.
The shoulder after stroke hurts during movement. Handle the arm carefully.

faqs.q: Can family members do passive exercises?
faqs.a: Yes, once taught. We train carers during home visits.

faqs.q: How is it different from stretching?
faqs.a: Range of motion moves through the range; stretching holds at the end.

exercises.title: Pediatric Strengthening
exercises.summary: Strengthening exercises for children with low tone and developmental conditions. Play-based ideas from Physiosolution pediatric physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Progressive, enjoyable strengthening improves function without feeling like exercise. You will often see it in our programmes for down syndrome, autism and cerebral palsy, and it features in our pediatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit to stand from small chairs during games.
Stepping up and down from a step or low bench.
Wheelbarrow walking to build arm and trunk strength.
Jumping, hopping and climbing play equipment.
Bridging and superman positions made into games.
exercises.howMuch: Short daily sessions of 15 to 20 minutes.
warnings: In muscular dystrophy, fatigue or soreness lasts more than a day. Exercise must be carefully dosed.

faqs.q: Is strength training safe for children?
faqs.a: Yes, when supervised and appropriate for age.

faqs.q: How do I keep it fun?
faqs.a: Turn it into games, challenges and rewards.

exercises.title: Pediatric Stretching
exercises.summary: Stretching exercises for children with cerebral palsy, clubfoot and torticollis. How parents can help, from Physiosolution pediatric physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Tight muscles can limit movement and lead to contractures as children grow. Regular stretching helps maintain range. It is a regular part of rehab plans for clubfoot, torticollis and cerebral palsy, and it features in our pediatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Choose a calm time, such as after a bath.
Hold the limb above and below the joint.
Move slowly to a gentle stretch and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
Common stretches: calves, hamstrings, hip adductors, and neck side bending in torticollis.
Keep it playful with songs or counting.
exercises.howMuch: Daily, as prescribed.
warnings: The child cries in pain during stretches.

faqs.q: Should stretches hurt?
faqs.a: No. They should be gentle and comfortable.

faqs.q: Can stretching replace splints?
faqs.a: Sometimes both are needed.

exercises.title: Pelvic Mobility Exercises
exercises.summary: Pelvic mobility exercises for pelvic girdle pain and pregnancy. Gentle movements from Physiosolution women's health physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Movement reduces stiffness in the pelvic joints and helps overactive muscles relax. You will often see it in our programmes for pelvic organ prolapse, tailbone pain and sacralization, and it features in our women's health physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Pelvic tilts in lying, sitting or on a ball.
Pelvic circles sitting on a birthing ball.
Cat cow on hands and knees.
Hip rolls: knees bent, let them fall gently side to side.
Child's pose with wide knees.
exercises.howMuch: 5 to 10 minutes daily.
warnings: Pelvic pain makes walking or turning in bed difficult. Specific treatment helps.

faqs.q: Is pelvic girdle pain normal in pregnancy?
faqs.a: It's common but treatable, so it shouldn't be ignored.

faqs.q: Can I use a gym ball?
faqs.a: Yes, if you feel steady on it.

exercises.title: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.summary: Pelvic tilt exercise for lower back pain, pregnancy and postnatal recovery. How to do it, reps and mistakes from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Small, controlled movement of the lumbar spine eases stiffness and muscle guarding. The backward tilt gently switches on the lower abdominal muscles, which helps build body awareness for later core work. It is a regular part of rehab plans for lumbar spondylosis, disc bulge and spondylolisthesis, and it features in our lower back pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip width apart.
Tighten your lower tummy gently and flatten your lower back into the floor by tilting the pelvis backwards.
Hold for 5 seconds and breathe normally.
Relax, then let the lower back arch slightly off the floor.
Move smoothly between the two positions.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 times a day. It can also be done sitting or standing against a wall.
commonMistakes: Pushing through the feet and lifting the buttocks.
Holding the breath.
warnings: Leg pain or numbness increases during the exercise.

faqs.q: Can I do pelvic tilts while pregnant?
faqs.a: Yes. After the first trimester, many women find them more comfortable on hands and knees or against a wall rather than lying flat.

faqs.q: How soon after childbirth?
faqs.a: Gentle pelvic tilts are usually fine within days of an uncomplicated delivery. After a caesarean, follow your doctor's guidance.

faqs.q: What are pelvic tilts?
faqs.a: Pelvic tilts gently rock the pelvis to flatten and arch the lower back, usually lying on your back with knees bent.

faqs.q: How are pelvic tilts performed?
faqs.a: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart. Breathe out and gently tighten your lower stomach as you flatten your lower back into the floor. The pelvis tilts backwards slightly. Hold for 3 to 5 seconds, breathing normally. Relax, then let the lower back arch a little as the pelvis tilts forward. Repeat 10 times, slowly.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of pelvic tilts?
faqs.a: They ease lower back stiffness and pain, activate the deep core and are safe early in rehab and in pregnancy. They are often part of rehab for lumbar spondylosis, disc bulge and spondylolisthesis.

faqs.q: Which muscles do pelvic tilts target?
faqs.a: The deep abdominals, especially transversus abdominis, and the lower back muscles.

exercises.title: Pendulum Exercise
exercises.summary: Pendulum exercise for shoulder pain, frozen shoulder and after surgery. Correct technique and duration from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Letting the arm hang and sway gently separates the joint surfaces slightly and moves the joint through small arcs. It reduces stiffness and pain with very little muscle effort. You will often see it in our programmes for rotator cuff injury, shoulder dislocation and shoulder and arm fractures, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Stand beside a table and lean forward, supporting yourself with your good hand on the table.
Let the painful arm hang straight down, completely relaxed.
Shift your body weight gently so the arm swings forwards and backwards, then side to side, then in small circles.
The movement should come from your body, not from lifting the arm.
Gradually make the circles a little bigger if comfortable.
exercises.howMuch: 30 seconds to 1 minute in each direction, 3 to 4 times a day.
commonMistakes: Using the shoulder muscles to swing the arm.
Standing too upright, so the arm doesn't hang freely.
warnings: Pain increases steadily during or after the exercise.
After surgery, you haven't yet been cleared by your surgeon for this exercise.

faqs.q: Can I do pendulums after rotator cuff surgery?
faqs.a: Often yes, early on, but follow your surgeon's protocol.

faqs.q: Should I hold a weight?
faqs.a: Not usually. The aim is relaxed movement.

faqs.q: What is the pendulum exercise?
faqs.a: The pendulum exercise lets the arm hang and swing gently in small circles while leaning forward, moving the shoulder without muscle effort.

faqs.q: How is the pendulum exercise performed?
faqs.a: Stand beside a table and lean on it with your good hand. Bend forward at the hips so your body is roughly at 45 to 90 degrees. Let your painful arm hang straight down, completely relaxed. Gently shift your weight side to side and forward and back so the arm swings like a pendulum. Then sway in small circles, clockwise and anticlockwise. Keep going for 30 to 60 seconds in each direction.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the pendulum exercise?
faqs.a: It eases pain and stiffness early after injury, surgery or in frozen shoulder, keeping the joint moving without strain. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder dislocation and shoulder and arm fractures.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the pendulum exercise target?
faqs.a: It relaxes the shoulder muscles; movement comes mainly from body sway rather than muscle work.

exercises.title: Piriformis Stretch
exercises.summary: Piriformis and glute stretch for buttock pain and sciatica. Figure-four and knee-to-shoulder versions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Tight deep hip rotators cause buttock ache and can irritate the sciatic nerve. Stretching reduces tension. You will often see it in our programmes for lumbar spondylosis, trochanteric bursitis and hip osteoarthritis, and it features in our sciatica physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Figure four: lie on your back with knees bent. Cross the right ankle over the left knee.
Draw the left thigh towards your chest until you feel a stretch in the right buttock. Hold 30 seconds.
Glute stretch: lie on your back and pull the right knee towards the left shoulder. Hold 30 seconds.
Switch sides.
exercises.howMuch: 2 to 3 holds each side, once or twice a day.
commonMistakes: Forcing the knee down.
warnings: You have hip replacement precautions against crossing the legs.
Leg pain spreads further.

faqs.q: Is sciatica caused by the piriformis?
faqs.a: Usually sciatica comes from the lower back. Piriformis involvement is less common.

faqs.q: Can I do this seated?
faqs.a: Yes: sit with the ankle on the opposite knee and lean forward with a straight back.

exercises.title: Plantar Fascia Stretch
exercises.summary: Plantar fascia stretch for heel pain and plantar fasciitis. Morning routine, rolling and towel stretches from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: The plantar fascia tightens overnight. Stretching it before standing reduces the pull on the heel with the first steps. It is a regular part of rehab plans for plantar fasciitis, ankle bone spur and flat foot, and it features in our sports physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit and cross the affected foot over the other knee.
Hold the base of your toes and pull them back towards your shin until you feel a stretch in the arch.
Hold 10 to 30 seconds.
Roll the arch over a frozen water bottle or ball for 1 to 2 minutes.
Do the stretch before getting out of bed in the morning.
exercises.howMuch: 3 holds, 3 times a day, including before first steps.
commonMistakes: Rolling so hard it bruises.
Only stretching and not strengthening.
warnings: Heel pain continues beyond 3 months or there's swelling, numbness or night pain.

faqs.q: How long does plantar fasciitis take to settle?
faqs.a: Many people improve over several months with stretching, strengthening and footwear changes.

faqs.q: Should I walk barefoot?
faqs.a: Supportive footwear usually helps in the early stages.

exercises.title: Post Fracture Exercises
exercises.summary: Exercises after a fracture: stages of recovery, what to expect and when to progress. Guidance from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Immobilisation causes stiffness and muscle loss. Exercise reverses these as healing allows. Our physiotherapists use it most often for wrist fracture, ankle fracture and hip fracture, and it features in our post-surgical rehabilitation programmes.
steps: While in a cast: move the joints that are free, such as fingers or toes.
After cast removal: gentle range of motion for the affected joint.
Weight bearing as allowed by your doctor.
Strengthening once movement returns.
Functional and balance training to finish.
exercises.howMuch: Early stage: short sessions several times a day. Later stages: daily programmes.
warnings: Pain suddenly increases, a deformity appears, or swelling, colour change and numbness develop.

faqs.q: How long does recovery take?
faqs.a: Bones heal in about 6 to 12 weeks, but strength and movement can take longer.

faqs.q: Can I exercise before the fracture heals?
faqs.a: Only what your doctor permits. Some movement is often allowed.

exercises.title: Post Hip Replacement Exercises
exercises.summary: Exercises after hip replacement surgery: stages, precautions and progression from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Strong glutes and hip muscles stabilise the new joint and prevent limping. You will often see it in our programmes for total hip replacement, hip osteoarthritis and hip fracture, and it features in our post-surgical rehabilitation programmes.
steps: Early: ankle pumps, buttock squeezes, quad sets, heel slides within limits.
Standing exercises: hip abduction, extension, mini squats holding on.
Walking practice with an aid, stair training.
Later: bridges, step ups, balance and walking distance.
Follow precautions on bending, crossing legs and twisting.
exercises.howMuch: 2 to 3 times a day early, then daily.
warnings: Sudden pain, a click with the leg looking shortened or turned, or calf swelling. Seek urgent help.

faqs.q: How long do hip precautions last?
faqs.a: Usually around 6 weeks, depending on your surgeon.

faqs.q: When can I drive?
faqs.a: Commonly 4 to 6 weeks, when cleared by your surgeon.

exercises.title: Post Knee Replacement Exercises
exercises.summary: Exercises after knee replacement surgery: week-by-week programme, range targets and tips from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: The new joint needs the muscles and soft tissues around it to move and control it. Consistent exercise determines the final result. Our physiotherapists use it most often for total knee replacement and knee osteoarthritis, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Week 1 to 2: ankle pumps, quad sets, straight leg raises, heel slides and knee extension stretches.
Week 2 to 6: short and long arc quads, sit to stand, walking with an aid, stairs.
Week 6 onwards: step ups, mini squats, balance work, cycling.
Ice and elevation help manage swelling.
exercises.howMuch: Exercises 2 to 3 times a day in the first weeks, then daily.
warnings: Knee bend is under 90 degrees at 2 weeks or isn't improving, or there's wound concern or calf swelling.

faqs.q: How much bend should I get?
faqs.a: Most people aim for around 110 to 120 degrees.

faqs.q: How long until I walk without a stick?
faqs.a: Often 4 to 8 weeks, depending on the person.

exercises.title: Post Stroke Exercises
exercises.summary: Exercises after stroke for arm, leg, balance and walking recovery. Home programme guidance from Physiosolution neuro physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Repeated practice drives neuroplasticity, the brain's ability to rewire. Intensity and repetition matter. You will often see it in our programmes for stroke and infantile hemiparesis, and it features in our neuro physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Range of motion for the affected arm and leg.
Weight shifting and sit to stand.
Arm and hand tasks: reaching, grasping, releasing.
Walking and balance practice.
Daily tasks practised with the affected side.
exercises.howMuch: As much practice as possible, spread through the day, as set by your physiotherapist.
warnings: New weakness, speech changes or facial drooping occur. Call emergency services.
The shoulder becomes painful; handle the affected arm carefully.

faqs.q: Is it too late if the stroke was years ago?
faqs.a: Improvement is still possible with focused practice.

faqs.q: Can therapy be done at home?
faqs.a: Yes. Home is often the best setting.

exercises.title: Post Surgery Exercises
exercises.summary: Exercises after surgery: stages, timelines and safety. Orthopaedic and spinal rehab guidance from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Early movement reduces complications like blood clots and chest infections. Graded rehab then restores function. Our physiotherapists use it most often for spinal fusion, discectomy and laminectomy, and it features in our post-surgical rehabilitation programmes.
steps: Day 1 onwards: ankle pumps, deep breathing, getting out of bed.
Early phase: gentle range of motion and muscle activation.
Middle phase: strengthening and walking progression.
Late phase: functional and sport-specific training.
Always follow your surgeon's restrictions.
exercises.howMuch: Short, frequent sessions early; longer programmes later.
warnings: Wound redness, discharge, fever, calf pain or new numbness occurs. Contact your surgical team.

faqs.q: Should I rest after surgery?
faqs.a: Early, safe movement generally helps recovery. Rest when needed.

faqs.q: Can you treat me at home after surgery?
faqs.a: Yes. Home visits are often ideal early on.

exercises.title: Postnatal Core Exercises
exercises.summary: Postnatal core exercises and core activation after childbirth and caesarean. Safe progression and diastasis recti tips from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Pregnancy stretches the abdominal wall. A graded programme restores support for the spine and pelvis. It is a regular part of rehab plans for urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse, and it features in our pregnancy and postnatal physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Breathing: diaphragmatic breathing with gentle pelvic floor lift on the out-breath.
Core activation: lying on your back, draw in the lower tummy slightly as you exhale.
Heel slides and leg lifts while keeping the tummy flat.
Glute bridges and side-lying exercises.
Progress to dead bugs and modified planks, watching for doming.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 minutes daily, progressing over weeks.
warnings: You have heaviness in the pelvis, leaking or doming of the tummy with exercise.

faqs.q: When can I start after a caesarean?
faqs.a: Gentle breathing and pelvic floor work can start early. Wait for medical clearance for more.

faqs.q: What is diastasis recti?
faqs.a: Separation of the abdominal muscles. Most improve with time and exercise.

exercises.title: Prenatal Mobility Exercises
exercises.summary: Prenatal mobility exercises for back and pelvic comfort in pregnancy. Safe routine and warning signs from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Changing posture and weight during pregnancy loads the back and pelvis. Gentle movement keeps joints comfortable. It is a regular part of rehab plans for urinary incontinence, and it features in our pregnancy and postnatal physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Cat cow on hands and knees.
Pelvic tilts against a wall.
Side-lying hip openers.
Seated hip and ankle circles.
Pelvic floor exercises and breathing.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 20 minutes daily if well.
warnings: You notice bleeding, fluid leakage, dizziness, chest pain or regular contractions. Stop and contact your maternity team.

faqs.q: Is exercise safe in pregnancy?
faqs.a: For most women with uncomplicated pregnancies, yes. Check with your doctor first.

faqs.q: Can I lie on my back?
faqs.a: After the first trimester, many women prefer side-lying or propped positions.

exercises.title: Pursed Lip Breathing
exercises.summary: Pursed lip breathing technique for breathlessness. When and how to use it, from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Slow exhalation against slight resistance helps prevent airway collapse and lets trapped air escape. It is a regular part of rehab plans for asthma and motor neuron disease, and it features in our geriatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Relax your shoulders.
Breathe in through your nose for 2 counts.
Purse your lips as if blowing out a candle.
Breathe out gently for 4 counts.
Use it during exertion, such as climbing stairs.
exercises.howMuch: Practise for a few minutes several times a day, then use it during activity.
warnings: Breathlessness is worsening, or you have chest pain. Seek medical care.

faqs.q: Is this useful in asthma attacks?
faqs.a: It can help calm breathing, but use your prescribed reliever and seek help if severe.

faqs.q: Should I force the air out?
faqs.a: No. It should be gentle and slow.

exercises.title: Quadriceps Sets
exercises.summary: Quadriceps sets (static quads) after knee surgery or injury. How to do them, reps and progress signs from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Swelling and pain inhibit the quadriceps, so it can feel impossible to tighten. Repeated static contractions restore activation, reduce muscle loss and help the knee straighten fully. It is a regular part of rehab plans for total knee replacement, ACL tear and meniscal injury, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit or lie with your leg straight, a small rolled towel under the knee.
Tighten the muscle on the front of your thigh to press the knee down into the towel.
Your kneecap should move slightly upwards.
Hold 5 to 10 seconds, then relax fully.
exercises.howMuch: 10 repetitions, every hour or two while awake in the early days after surgery, then 3 times a day.
commonMistakes: Tightening the buttocks instead of the thigh.
Holding the breath.
warnings: Calf pain, swelling or redness appears after surgery. It can indicate a blood clot.

faqs.q: I can't feel the muscle working. What now?
faqs.a: Put your hand on the thigh, look at it while trying, and try pulling your toes up at the same time. We can also use electrical stimulation.

faqs.q: When will I stop needing these?
faqs.a: Once you can do a straight leg raise without the knee bending.

exercises.title: Quadriceps Stretch
exercises.summary: Quadriceps stretch for knee pain and tight thighs. Standing and lying versions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Stretching the quadriceps improves knee bend and reduces tension through the kneecap and patellar tendon. It is a regular part of rehab plans for chondromalacia patella, patellar tendonitis and Osgood-Schlatter disease, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Stand holding a support with your left hand.
Bend your right knee and hold the ankle with your right hand.
Bring the heel towards your buttock, keeping knees together.
Tuck your pelvis slightly to increase the stretch at the front of the hip.
Hold 30 seconds and switch.
exercises.howMuch: 3 holds each leg, once or twice a day.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back.
Letting the knee drift out to the side.
warnings: Kneeling or bending is painful after a knee injury.

faqs.q: Can't reach my ankle?
faqs.a: Loop a towel around it, or do the stretch lying on your side.

faqs.q: Does this help Osgood-Schlatter?
faqs.a: Quadriceps flexibility is part of management, along with load changes.

exercises.title: Resistance Band Ankle Exercises
exercises.summary: Resistance band ankle exercises: dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion and eversion. Sets, reps and tips from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: After a sprain, the peroneal muscles that turn the foot out are often weak, which contributes to repeated sprains. Band work restores strength in every direction. It is a regular part of rehab plans for ankle sprain, ankle instability and ankle fracture, and it features in our sports physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit with your leg straight and a band looped around the ball of the foot.
Plantarflexion: hold both ends and point the foot down against the band.
Dorsiflexion: anchor the band in front and pull the foot up towards you.
Inversion: anchor the band to the outside and turn the sole of the foot inwards.
Eversion: anchor it to the inside and turn the sole outwards.
exercises.howMuch: 15 repetitions in each direction, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Rotating the whole leg instead of moving the ankle.
Letting the band snap back.
warnings: There's sharp pain on the outer ankle or the ankle gives way repeatedly.

faqs.q: Which direction matters most after a sprain?
faqs.a: Eversion, as the peroneal muscles protect against rolling the ankle.

faqs.q: When should balance work start?
faqs.a: Usually once standing is comfortable, alongside band work.

exercises.title: Resistance Band Exercises
exercises.summary: Resistance band exercises for home strengthening and rehab. How to choose a band, key exercises and progressions from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Bands allow gradual progression from light to strong resistance. Their tension increases through the movement, which suits controlled rehab exercises. Our physiotherapists use it most often for osteoporosis, knee osteoarthritis and rotator cuff injury, and it features in our geriatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Choose a band that lets you complete 12 to 15 controlled repetitions.
Anchor safely: under your foot, in a door anchor or around a sturdy post.
Key exercises: rows, chest press, shoulder rotations, leg press, side steps with band around knees, and ankle movements.
Move slowly, especially when returning to the start.
Progress to a stronger band when 15 repetitions feel easy.
exercises.howMuch: 2 to 3 sets of 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 days a week per muscle group.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap back.
Anchoring to something unstable.
warnings: The band is worn or cracked. Replace it before it snaps.

faqs.q: Are bands as effective as weights?
faqs.a: For general strength and rehab, studies show similar gains.

faqs.q: Which band should I buy?
faqs.a: A set of light, medium and heavy bands covers most needs.

exercises.title: Resistance Band Shoulder Exercises
exercises.summary: Resistance band shoulder exercises for strength and rehab. Rows, external rotation, pull-aparts and raises with sets and reps from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Band exercises strengthen the rotator cuff and shoulder blade muscles through range. Band tension increases as it stretches, which suits shoulder rehabilitation well. It is a regular part of rehab plans for rotator cuff injury, shoulder impingement and shoulder dislocation, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Rows: pull the band towards your ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades.
External and internal rotation: elbow at your side, rotate outwards and inwards against the band.
Pull-aparts: hold the band in front at shoulder height and pull the hands apart.
Front raise: stand on the band and lift the arm forward to shoulder height.
Scaption: stand on the band and lift the arm up and slightly out, thumb up.
exercises.howMuch: 12 to 15 repetitions of each, 2 to 3 sets, 3 to 4 days a week. Move to a stronger band when 15 repetitions feel easy.
commonMistakes: Letting the band snap back instead of returning slowly.
Choosing a band too strong to control.
warnings: Night pain or pain at rest increases.

faqs.q: Which band colour should I start with?
faqs.a: Colours vary by brand. Start with one that lets you finish 15 repetitions with good form.

faqs.q: Are bands as good as weights?
faqs.a: For rehabilitation, yes. For heavy strength goals, weights allow more load.

faqs.q: What are resistance band shoulder exercises?
faqs.a: Resistance band shoulder exercises use elastic bands to strengthen the shoulder in multiple directions.

faqs.q: How are resistance band shoulder exercises performed?
faqs.a: Resistance band shoulder exercises use elastic bands to strengthen the shoulder in multiple directions.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of resistance band shoulder exercises?
faqs.a: They build strength progressively at home, support rehab and prevent injury. They are often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder impingement and shoulder dislocation.

faqs.q: Which muscles do resistance band shoulder exercises target?
faqs.a: The rotator cuff, deltoid and shoulder blade muscles.

exercises.title: Respiratory Muscle Training
exercises.summary: Respiratory muscle training (inspiratory muscle training) for breathlessness. Who benefits and how it's done, from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Breathing muscles respond to training like other muscles. Stronger muscles make breathing feel less effortful. Our physiotherapists use it most often for asthma, spinal cord injury and motor neuron disease, and it features in our neuro physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit upright and set the device to the prescribed resistance.
Breathe out fully, then breathe in hard and fast through the device.
Breathe out gently.
Repeat for the set number of breaths.
exercises.howMuch: Typically 30 breaths, twice a day, as prescribed.
warnings: You have a history of lung collapse or recent chest surgery. The device may not be suitable.
In progressive neuromuscular conditions, training must be carefully dosed.

faqs.q: Is this suitable for everyone?
faqs.a: No. We assess first and set the resistance level.

faqs.q: How long until I notice benefit?
faqs.a: Often several weeks of consistent training.

exercises.title: Rolling Exercises
exercises.summary: Rolling exercises for babies and developmental delay. How to encourage rolling through play, from Physiosolution pediatric physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Rolling involves coordinating the head, trunk and limbs. Practice helps babies discover the movement. Our physiotherapists use it most often for down syndrome, cerebral palsy and infantile hemiparesis, and it features in our pediatric physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Place a toy just out of reach to one side.
As the baby reaches, gently guide the hip or shoulder to help them roll.
Practise to both sides.
Reduce your help as they learn.
exercises.howMuch: A few times during each play session.
warnings: Your baby rolls only to one side or isn't rolling by 7 months.

faqs.q: When should babies roll?
faqs.a: Most roll between 4 and 6 months, but ranges vary.

faqs.q: Should I worry if they skip rolling?
faqs.a: Discuss it if other milestones are also delayed.

exercises.title: Rotator Cuff Rehabilitation Exercises
exercises.summary: Rotator cuff rehabilitation exercises for tendinopathy, tears and after repair. Phases and progressions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Progressive loading builds tendon capacity. After repair, early protection allows healing before loading starts. You will often see it in our programmes for rotator cuff injury, supraspinatus tendinitis and shoulder impingement, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Early after surgery: sling, pendulums, passive range by a therapist.
Active-assisted and active range as allowed.
Isometrics, then band strengthening.
Progressive strength and overhead function.
For tendinopathy without surgery, start with isometrics and progress load.
exercises.howMuch: Daily, with strength sessions 3 times a week.
warnings: Sudden loss of strength or a pop after surgery.

faqs.q: How long after repair until I can lift?
faqs.a: Light use at several weeks, heavier lifting often after 3 to 4 months.

faqs.q: Can tendinopathy heal without surgery?
faqs.a: Most improve with exercise over about 3 months.

exercises.title: Rotator Cuff Strengthening
exercises.summary: Rotator cuff strengthening exercises. External rotation, side-lying rotation, scaption and progressions, explained by Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Progressive loading improves tendon capacity and muscle strength. Most rotator cuff tendinopathies improve with a well structured programme over 8 to 12 weeks. Our physiotherapists use it most often for rotator cuff injury, supraspinatus tendinitis and shoulder impingement, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Side-lying external rotation: lie on your side with a towel under the top elbow. Holding a light weight, rotate the forearm up towards the ceiling and lower slowly.
Band external rotation at 90 degrees: once basic rotation is strong, raise the elbow to shoulder height and rotate the forearm up.
Scaption: lift the arms up and slightly forward with thumbs up, to shoulder height.
Prone horizontal abduction: lie face down, arm hanging, lift it out sideways with thumb up.
exercises.howMuch: 8 to 15 repetitions, 3 sets, 3 days a week. Aim for the last few repetitions to feel hard but controlled.
commonMistakes: Using weights that are too heavy, so bigger muscles take over.
Rushing the lowering phase.
warnings: Weakness is sudden or severe after an injury. This may be a significant tear needing imaging.

faqs.q: How long until my rotator cuff is stronger?
faqs.a: Strength gains start in weeks; tendon improvement typically takes 3 months.

faqs.q: Some pain during exercise okay?
faqs.a: Mild discomfort that settles within 24 hours is usually acceptable in tendon rehab. We'll set your limits.

faqs.q: What is the rotator cuff strengthening?
faqs.a: Rotator cuff strengthening is a set of band and weight exercises that build the four small muscles stabilising the shoulder.

faqs.q: How is the rotator cuff strengthening performed?
faqs.a: Isometrics when movement is painful: steady holds against a wall. Rotation with the elbow at the side, using light bands or weights. Lifting in the scapular plane (slightly forward of straight out to the side), up to shoulder height. Rotation with the arm lifted out to the side, then overhead and functional strength.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the rotator cuff strengthening?
faqs.a: They reduce shoulder pain, prevent injury and support recovery after rotator cuff injury or surgery. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, supraspinatus tendinitis and shoulder impingement.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the rotator cuff strengthening target?
faqs.a: The supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis.

exercises.title: Scapular Retraction
exercises.summary: Scapular retraction exercise for posture, neck and shoulder pain. How to do it, reps and resistance band progression from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: Rounded shoulders stretch the muscles between the shoulder blades and change how the shoulder joint moves. Retraction retrains the middle and lower trapezius and rhomboids, which improves posture and gives the shoulder a stable base. You will often see it in our programmes for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and cervical spondylosis, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed by your sides.
Gently draw your shoulder blades back and slightly down, as if sliding them into your back pockets.
Keep your neck long and don't shrug.
Hold 5 seconds and release slowly.
Progress by holding a resistance band in both hands, elbows bent at 90 degrees, and pulling the band apart as you squeeze.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets, once a day. Quick sets during the workday help build the habit.
commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up.
Arching the lower back or pushing the ribs forward.
Squeezing too hard. Moderate effort is enough.
warnings: You get sharp pain in the front of the shoulder.

faqs.q: Will this fix my posture?
faqs.a: It helps, but posture also depends on your workstation, breaks and overall activity.

faqs.q: Can I do it at my desk?
faqs.a: Yes. It's one of the easiest exercises to do while seated.

faqs.q: What is the scapular retraction?
faqs.a: Scapular retraction is squeezing the shoulder blades gently back and down to activate the muscles that control shoulder posture.

faqs.q: How is the scapular retraction performed?
faqs.a: Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed by your sides. Gently draw your shoulder blades back and slightly down, as if tucking them into your back pockets. Hold for 5 seconds without shrugging or arching your lower back. Relax and repeat 10 times. ## Progressions.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the scapular retraction?
faqs.a: It improves rounded shoulder posture, supports neck and shoulder rehab and is a foundation for shoulder strengthening. It is often part of rehab for cervical spondylosis, shoulder impingement and rotator cuff injury.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the scapular retraction target?
faqs.a: The middle and lower trapezius and rhomboids.

exercises.title: Scapular Stabilization Exercises
exercises.summary: Scapular stabilization exercises for shoulder pain and posture. Prone Y, T and W raises and rows explained by Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: The shoulder blade must tilt, rotate and glide as the arm moves. Poor control changes the load on the rotator cuff and the joint. These exercises target the lower and middle trapezius, rhomboids and serratus anterior. You will often see it in our programmes for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and shoulder dislocation, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Rows: pull a band anchored in front of you towards your ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades back and down.
Prone T: lie face down, arms out to the sides, thumbs up. Squeeze the shoulder blades and lift the arms slightly.
Prone Y: same position with arms overhead in a Y shape. Lift slightly, keeping the neck long.
Prone W: elbows bent, arms in a W shape. Lift and squeeze.
Hold each lift 2 to 3 seconds.
exercises.howMuch: 10 repetitions of each, 2 sets, once a day. Start without weights.
commonMistakes: Lifting the head or arching the back.
Shrugging instead of squeezing down and back.
Lifting too high, which switches on the wrong muscles.
warnings: Any lift causes pinching pain in the front or top of the shoulder.

faqs.q: Do I need a gym for these?
faqs.a: No. A band and a bed or floor are enough.

faqs.q: What is scapular winging?
faqs.a: The shoulder blade lifting away from the ribs, often from weak serratus anterior or nerve injury. It needs assessment.

faqs.q: What are scapular stabilization exercises?
faqs.a: Scapular stabilisation exercises train the muscles that control the shoulder blade so it moves smoothly and supports the arm.

faqs.q: How are scapular stabilization exercises performed?
faqs.a: Scapular stabilisation exercises train the muscles that control the shoulder blade so it moves smoothly and supports the arm.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of scapular stabilization exercises?
faqs.a: They reduce shoulder pain and impingement, improve posture and prepare the shoulder for lifting and overhead activity. They are often part of rehab for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and shoulder dislocation.

faqs.q: Which muscles do scapular stabilization exercises target?
faqs.a: The serratus anterior, trapezius (middle and lower) and rhomboids.

exercises.title: Serratus Anterior Exercises
exercises.summary: Serratus anterior exercises for shoulder blade winging and impingement. Punches, push-up plus and wall slides from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: The serratus rotates the shoulder blade upward and holds it against the ribs. Training it improves overhead movement and pushing strength. Our physiotherapists use it most often for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and Sprengel's shoulder, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Supine punch: lie on your back holding a light weight with the arm straight up. Punch towards the ceiling so the shoulder blade lifts off the floor, then lower slightly.
Wall push-up plus: do a wall push-up, then at the top push further so the shoulder blades spread apart.
Wall slides with foam roller or towel: forearms on the wall, roll up while pressing forward.
Progress to push-up plus on a table or the floor.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions of each, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows during the punch or the plus.
Shrugging.
warnings: The shoulder blade sticks out markedly or you have new weakness. Nerve injury needs assessment.

faqs.q: What causes a winging shoulder blade?
faqs.a: Often weak serratus anterior, sometimes injury to the long thoracic nerve.

faqs.q: Can I do push-ups?
faqs.a: Yes, once the wall and table versions are controlled.

faqs.q: What are serratus anterior exercises?
faqs.a: Serratus anterior exercises, such as wall slides and push-up plus, strengthen the muscle that holds the shoulder blade against the ribcage.

faqs.q: How are serratus anterior exercises performed?
faqs.a: Serratus anterior exercises, such as wall slides and push-up plus, strengthen the muscle that holds the shoulder blade against the ribcage.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of serratus anterior exercises?
faqs.a: They help prevent shoulder blade winging, reduce impingement pain and improve overhead movement. They are often part of rehab for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and Sprengel's shoulder.

faqs.q: Which muscles do serratus anterior exercises target?
faqs.a: The serratus anterior, with support from the trapezius.

exercises.title: Short Arc Quads
exercises.summary: Short arc quad exercise for knee strength after surgery or injury. Steps and reps from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Final knee extension is controlled mainly by the inner part of the quadriceps. This exercise targets it with low joint load. Our physiotherapists use it most often for total knee replacement, ACL tear and knee osteoarthritis, and it features in our knee pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Lie or sit with your leg out straight and a rolled towel or coffee tin under the knee.
Keep the back of the knee on the roll.
Lift the heel until the knee is fully straight.
Hold 3 to 5 seconds, then lower slowly.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets, once or twice a day.
commonMistakes: Lifting the thigh off the roll.
Not reaching full straightening.
warnings: Sharp pain behind the kneecap persists.

faqs.q: Why the towel roll?
faqs.a: It limits the movement to the last part of straightening, where strength is often lacking.

faqs.q: How do I progress?
faqs.a: Add an ankle weight, then move on to long arc quads.

exercises.title: Short Foot Exercise
exercises.summary: Short foot exercise for flat feet and arch support. How to do it correctly and progressions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: The intrinsic foot muscles form a dynamic arch support. Training them improves foot control during standing and walking. You will often see it in our programmes for flat foot, plantar fasciitis and posterior tibial tendon dysfunction, and it features in our sports physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit with your foot flat on the floor.
Without curling your toes, slide the ball of your foot towards your heel so the arch rises.
Keep the big toe pressed down.
Hold 5 seconds and relax.
Progress to standing on both feet, then on one foot.
exercises.howMuch: 10 holds, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Curling the toes instead of lifting the arch.
Lifting the big toe.
warnings: Flat feet are painful and worsening, especially one side. Tibialis posterior dysfunction needs assessment.

faqs.q: Will this fix flat feet?
faqs.a: It can improve arch control and symptoms. It won't change bone structure.

faqs.q: It's hard to feel. Is that normal?
faqs.a: Yes, at first. It gets easier within a couple of weeks.

exercises.title: Shoulder Abduction
exercises.summary: Shoulder abduction exercise for rotator cuff and impingement pain. Safe technique, reps and progressions from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Abduction uses the supraspinatus and deltoid working with the shoulder blade muscles. Retraining it restores the ability to reach sideways and lift objects away from the body. Our physiotherapists use it most often for shoulder impingement, rotator cuff injury and supraspinatus tendinitis, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Stand tall with the arm by your side, thumb pointing forward.
Lift the arm out to the side and slightly forward, in the plane of the shoulder blade (about 30 degrees in front of straight sideways).
Rise to shoulder height or as high as is comfortable without shrugging.
Lower slowly over 3 seconds.
Add a light weight or band when you can do 15 smooth repetitions.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Shrugging or leaning the trunk away.
Lifting with the thumb pointing down, which can pinch the shoulder.
Dropping the arm quickly.
warnings: A painful arc between shoulder and head height persists or worsens after two weeks.

faqs.q: What is a painful arc?
faqs.a: Pain in the middle part of lifting the arm sideways, easing above and below. It's typical of impingement.

faqs.q: Is it fine to lift above shoulder height?
faqs.a: If comfortable, yes. We usually add height as control improves.

faqs.q: What is the shoulder abduction?
faqs.a: Shoulder abduction is lifting the arm out to the side and up.

faqs.q: How is the shoulder abduction performed?
faqs.a: Shoulder abduction is lifting the arm out to the side and up.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the shoulder abduction?
faqs.a: It restores the ability to lift the arm sideways for dressing and daily tasks. It is often part of rehab for shoulder impingement, supraspinatus tendinitis and rotator cuff injury.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the shoulder abduction target?
faqs.a: The middle deltoid and supraspinatus.

exercises.title: Shoulder Circles
exercises.summary: Shoulder circles and shoulder rolls to relieve stiffness and tension. How to do them and when, from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Moving the shoulder girdle through its full range increases blood flow, loosens tight muscles and reminds the body to leave the hunched position. You will often see it in our programmes for cervical spondylosis and fibromyalgia syndrome, and it features in our neck pain physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed.
Lift both shoulders up towards your ears, roll them back, down and forward in a smooth circle.
Make the circle as large as is comfortable, especially the backward part.
After 10 circles backwards, do 5 forwards.
For a larger version, place your fingertips on your shoulders and draw circles with your elbows.
exercises.howMuch: 10 backward and 5 forward circles, every hour or two during desk work.
commonMistakes: Rushing through small, tense circles.
Holding your breath.
warnings: Circles produce grinding with pain or catching in the shoulder joint.

faqs.q: Why more backwards than forwards?
faqs.a: Most people spend the day with shoulders rounded forward, so the backward movement is the more useful one.

faqs.q: Are these enough on their own?
faqs.a: They are a good break exercise. Strength work is needed for lasting change.

faqs.q: What are shoulder circles?
faqs.a: Shoulder circles roll the shoulders forward and backward in slow circles.

faqs.q: How are shoulder circles performed?
faqs.a: Sit or stand tall with arms relaxed by your sides. Lift both shoulders up towards your ears. Draw them back, squeezing the shoulder blades together. Lower them down, then bring them forward to complete the circle. Do 10 circles backwards, then 10 forwards.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of shoulder circles?
faqs.a: They loosen stiff shoulders and upper back and relieve tension from sitting. They are often part of rehab for cervical spondylosis, fibromyalgia syndrome and ankylosing spondylitis.

faqs.q: Which muscles do shoulder circles target?
faqs.a: The trapezius, rhomboids and deltoid work gently.

exercises.title: Shoulder Extension
exercises.summary: Shoulder extension exercise for stiffness and strength. Assisted and resisted versions with reps from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Extension combines shoulder joint movement with shoulder blade control. The exercise restores range and strengthens the back of the shoulder. You will often see it in our programmes for shoulder and arm fractures, rotator cuff injury and shoulder arthropathy, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Assisted: stand holding a stick behind your back with both hands. Lift the stick backwards away from your body.
Active: stand tall and move one arm straight back, keeping the elbow straight and the trunk still.
Resisted: anchor a band in front of you at waist height. Holding it with a straight arm, pull it back past your hip.
Return slowly.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Bending forward at the waist to make the arm look higher.
Rolling the shoulder forward at the end of the movement.
warnings: Pain at the front of the shoulder increases after sessions.

faqs.q: Why is reaching behind my back so hard?
faqs.a: It combines extension and internal rotation, both of which stiffen early in many shoulder conditions.

faqs.q: Can I use a towel instead of a stick?
faqs.a: Yes, for gentle assisted stretching.

faqs.q: What is the shoulder extension?
faqs.a: Shoulder extension is moving the arm backward behind the body, often with a resistance band.

faqs.q: How is the shoulder extension performed?
faqs.a: Shoulder extension is moving the arm backward behind the body, often with a resistance band.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the shoulder extension?
faqs.a: It restores reaching behind, improves posture and strengthens the back of the shoulder. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder arthropathy and shoulder and arm fractures.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the shoulder extension target?
faqs.a: The latissimus dorsi, posterior deltoid and teres major.

exercises.title: Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.summary: Shoulder external rotation exercise with a resistance band. Steps, reps and mistakes for rotator cuff and shoulder pain from Physiosolution.
exercises.whatItDoes: The rotator cuff controls the head of the upper arm bone. Weak external rotators allow it to ride up and pinch, and reduce stability after dislocation. You will often see it in our programmes for rotator cuff injury, shoulder impingement and shoulder dislocation, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Stand side-on to a door with a band anchored at elbow height, holding it in the hand furthest from the door.
Keep the elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your side. A rolled towel between elbow and ribs helps.
Rotate the forearm outwards away from your belly, keeping the elbow in place.
Return slowly over 3 seconds.
For stiffness, do it assisted: lie on your back holding a stick and use the other arm to push the hand outwards.
exercises.howMuch: 12 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets, once a day.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the body.
Twisting the trunk instead of rotating the shoulder.
Using a band that is too strong.
warnings: Pain increases at night after starting the exercise.

faqs.q: Why a towel under the arm?
faqs.a: It keeps the elbow in position and slightly improves the muscle's working position.

faqs.q: Is external rotation lost in frozen shoulder?
faqs.a: Yes, it is usually the most restricted movement.

faqs.q: What is the shoulder external rotation?
faqs.a: Shoulder external rotation turns the forearm outward with the elbow at your side, usually against a band.

faqs.q: How is the shoulder external rotation performed?
faqs.a: Stand side-on to a door with a band anchored at elbow height. Hold the band in the hand farthest from the door. Keep your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side. A rolled towel between elbow and ribs helps. Rotate the forearm outwards, away from your stomach, keeping the elbow in place. Return slowly. 2 to 3 sets of 10 to 15.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the shoulder external rotation?
faqs.a: It strengthens the rotator cuff, helps impingement and instability and restores outward movement in frozen shoulder. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder impingement and shoulder dislocation.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the shoulder external rotation target?
faqs.a: The infraspinatus and teres minor.

exercises.title: Shoulder Flexion
exercises.summary: Shoulder flexion exercises for stiffness and weakness. Assisted, active and resisted versions with reps from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Restoring overhead reach is a key goal after most shoulder problems. Flexion exercises rebuild range first, then the strength to control the arm at height. It is a regular part of rehab plans for rotator cuff injury, shoulder and arm fractures and shoulder dislocation, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Assisted: lie on your back holding a stick with both hands. Use the good arm to help lift the stick overhead as far as comfortable.
Active: standing or lying, raise the arm forward with the thumb pointing up. Go as high as you can control without shrugging.
Resisted: hold a light weight or loop a band under your foot and lift forward to shoulder height.
Lower slowly each time.
exercises.howMuch: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 sets, once or twice a day. Stay at each stage until it's comfortable before progressing.
commonMistakes: Hitching the shoulder up towards the ear.
Arching the back to get the arm higher.
Progressing to weights before full active range is controlled.
warnings: You feel sharp pinching at the top of the shoulder that doesn't ease.

faqs.q: Why is lying down easier?
faqs.a: Lying reduces the effect of gravity, so less strength is needed to move the arm.

faqs.q: How high should I go?
faqs.a: As high as you can move smoothly. Range improves over weeks.

faqs.q: What is the shoulder flexion?
faqs.a: Shoulder flexion is raising the arm forward and up overhead, done actively or with assistance.

faqs.q: How is the shoulder flexion performed?
faqs.a: Shoulder flexion is raising the arm forward and up overhead, done actively or with assistance.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the shoulder flexion?
faqs.a: It restores the ability to reach forward and overhead for daily tasks. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder impingement and shoulder arthropathy.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the shoulder flexion target?
faqs.a: The anterior deltoid, with help from the rotator cuff and serratus anterior.

exercises.title: Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.summary: Shoulder internal rotation exercises for stiffness and strength. Band exercise and towel stretch explained by Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Strength in internal rotation stabilises the front of the shoulder. Range in internal rotation is needed for dressing and personal care. Our physiotherapists use it most often for rotator cuff injury, shoulder arthropathy and shoulder dislocation, and it features in our frozen shoulder physiotherapy programmes.
steps: Strength: stand side-on to a door with a band anchored at elbow height, holding it in the hand nearest the door.
Keep the elbow tucked at your side, bent to 90 degrees, and pull the band inwards across your belly.
Return slowly.
Stretch: hold a towel over one shoulder with the top hand and grasp the bottom end behind your back with the stiff arm. Pull the towel up with the top hand to slide the lower hand higher.
exercises.howMuch: Strength: 12 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 sets. Stretch: 5 slow repetitions with a 10 second hold, twice a day.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbow leave the side.
Forcing the towel stretch into pain.
warnings: The towel stretch produces sharp pain rather than stretch.

faqs.q: Why is internal rotation slow to come back?
faqs.a: It depends on the back of the joint capsule, which is often among the last structures to loosen.

faqs.q: Is the sleeper stretch the same?
faqs.a: It's another internal rotation stretch, but it can irritate some shoulders. We advise individually.

faqs.q: What is the shoulder internal rotation?
faqs.a: Shoulder internal rotation turns the forearm inward towards the stomach with the elbow at your side, often against a band.

faqs.q: How is the shoulder internal rotation performed?
faqs.a: Stand side-on to a door with a band anchored at elbow height, holding it in the hand nearest the door. Keep the elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side. Rotate the forearm inwards across your stomach. Return slowly. 2 to 3 sets of 10 to 15.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of the shoulder internal rotation?
faqs.a: It strengthens the front of the shoulder and helps reaching behind the back. It is often part of rehab for rotator cuff injury, shoulder arthropathy and shoulder dislocation.

faqs.q: Which muscles does the shoulder internal rotation target?
faqs.a: The subscapularis, with help from the pectoralis major and latissimus dorsi.

exercises.title: Shoulder Isometric Exercises
exercises.summary: Shoulder isometric exercises for rotator cuff pain and early rehab. Five directions, holds and effort level from Physiosolution physiotherapists.
exercises.whatItDoes: Isometric contractions strengthen the rotator cuff and deltoid and can give short-term pain relief in tendinopathy. You will often see it in our programmes for rotator cuff injury, supraspinatus tendinitis and biceps tendonitis, and it features in our shoulder pain physiotherapy programmes.
